DISCOVERY 612, TENTATIVE RULING ADOPTED. DEFENDANTS KIMPTON HOTEL AND RESTAURANT GROUP, LLC'S MOTION TO COMPEL PLAINTIFF TO RESPOND TO DISCOVERY, AND TO PROVIDE FURTHER DISCOVERY RESPONSES IS GRANTED. LATE OPPOSITION HAS BEEN CONSIDERED. PLAINTIFF'S FAILURE TO RESPOND FULLY WAS A MISUSE OF THE DISCOVERY PROCESS. SANCTIONS ARE AWARDED AGAINST PLAINTIFF'S COUNSEL IN THE AMOUNT OF $690, TO BE PAID WITHIN 30 DAYS OF NOTICE OF THIS ORDER. LAW AND MOTION 301, THE COURT ADOPTED ITS TENTATIVE RULING AS FOLLOWS : DEFENDANTS KIMPTON HOTEL & RESTAURANT GROUP, L.L.C., HECTOR ROMERO AND DAVID WALOVICH'S MOTION FOR SUMMARY JUDGMENT IS DENIED. THERE ARE TRIABLE ISSUES OF MATERIAL FACT AS TO WHETHER DEFENDANTS DEFAMED THE PLAINTIFF AND PUBLISHED THE DEFAMATORY STATEMENTS TO PLAINTIFF'S CO-WORKERS AS SHE WAS ESCORTED BACK AND FORTH BETWEEN AN OFFICE AND THE DINING ROOM, CONDUCT THAT GOES BEYOND SUPERVISORY CRITICISM AND IS NOT A RISK REASONABLY ENCOMPASSED WITHIN THE EMPLOYMENT RELATIONSHIP. BASED ON WALOVICH'S INTERROGATORY RESPONSES AND DECLARATIONS, THERE IS ALSO A TRIABLE ISSUE OF MATERIAL FACT AS TO WHETHER HE WAS EMPLOYED BY KIMPTON AT THE RELEVANT TIME. PREVAILING PARTY IS TO PREPARE A FORM OF ORDER PURSUANT TO CCP 437 C(G). JUDGE: PETER J. BUSCH, REPORTER: CAROL KAREN, CSR# 8189 (301/PJB)
